title: Tuned-Lens-Style Affine Alignment for Encoder Truncation in Whisper ASR: An Empirical Investigation

contributions.purpose: Test whether tuned-lens-style representation alignment can make Whisper encoder truncation practical for speedup.
contributions.mechanism: Systematic investigation training affine and MLP translators to map truncated encoder states to the expected final-layer distribution across multiple depths (L in {20,24,28}).
contributions.evaluation: Provides a systematic study across multiple truncation depths on Whisper-large-v2 (encoder = 68% of inference latency).
contributions.domain: Whisper encoder-decoder ASR / encoder truncation for speedup
contributions.source_quote: First, we provide a systematic investigation of tuned-lens-style affine and MLP alignment for Whisper encoder truncation across multiple depths (L in {20,24,28}).

contributions.purpose: Characterize the tradeoff between truncation depth and speedup.
contributions.mechanism: Measuring WER and speedup at different truncation depths with the trained translators.
contributions.evaluation: Fundamental depth-speedup tradeoff: depths yielding meaningful speedup (>=1.2x) produce catastrophic WER (>100%), while the shallowest non-catastrophic depth (WER 18.90% at L=28) provides no speedup.
contributions.source_quote: Second, we identify a fundamental depth-speedup tradeoff: truncation depths that yield meaningful speedup (>=1.2x) produce catastrophic WER (>100%), while the shallowest depth with non-catastrophic WER (18.90% at L=28) provides no speedup.

contributions.purpose: Explain why the tuned-lens analogy fails for encoder-decoder ASR.
contributions.mechanism: Analysis contrasting cross-attention alignment requirements with vocabulary prediction in decoder-only models.
contributions.evaluation: Concludes cross-attention has stricter alignment requirements than vocabulary prediction, so the tuned-lens analogy does not transfer to encoder-decoder ASR.
contributions.source_quote: Third, we analyze why the tuned-lens analogy fails for encoder-decoder ASR: cross-attention has stricter alignment requirements than vocabulary prediction in decoder-only models.

self_declared_provenance.quote: The tuned lens (Belrose et al., 2023) offers a promising hypothesis: in autoregressive language models, learned affine transformations can align intermediate representations to the final layer... a lightweight translator could bridge this gap without full model retraining.
Our work applies the tuned lens concept to encoder-decoder ASR, testing whether affine alignment can bridge the gap between intermediate and final encoder representations for cross-attention.

Unlike these approaches that train dedicated exit branches, we investigate whether tuned-lens-style alignment alone can enable encoder truncation in the encoder-decoder Whisper architecture, where the challenge is aligning representations for cross-attention rather than direct classification.

notes: EXPLICIT NEGATIVE-RESULT PAPER: the tuned-lens analogy does NOT transfer to encoder-decoder ASR. All usable truncation depths either give catastrophic WER (>100%) or zero speedup; no configuration achieves both acceptable WER and speedup. Title itself frames it as 'An Empirical Investigation' documenting a negative finding.
